LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Pittsburgh is 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay, while New Orleans is 2-4 after beating the Giants 34-27. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn't easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It's the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. Courtesy of the team's Week 7 practice report, the Steelers revealed that Dowdle was limited with a new knee injury. The severity of the surprise setback and when he suffered the injury are unknown, but his limited participation is worth something. Dowdle, who signed with the Steelers in March 2026, was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard seasons with two different teams: the Dallas Cowboys (2024) and Carolina Panthers (2025). away.headline: Steelers starter dealing with new injury ahead of Week 7 in Paris
away.blurb: Taking a look at the Steelers' Week 7 injury report, starting edge rusher Alex Highsmith was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice with a groin issue. Although there's reason for concern with Highsmith's history of groin injuries, his limited participation was better than not being at practice at all. Highsmith, who was drafted by the Steelers in the third round of the 2020 NFL Draft, has quietly emerged as one of the league's most underrated edge rushers, recording 48 sacks, 10 forced fumbles, 348 combined tackles, and 69 tackles for loss in 96 games. We're uncertain when exactly Highsmith suffered the setback, and the severity of the injury is unknown, but the Steelers have plenty of capable edge rushers in Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer ready to step up to the plate if their number is called upon. away.headline: Steelers week 7 Thursday injury report: Latest updates and analysis
away.blurb: The Saints currently sit third in the NFC South, just 1.5 games out of first place. Meanwhile, the Steelers are only half a game behind the division leaders in the AFC North. Both teams also have injury concerns heading into Sunday’s matchup. Pittsburgh could get some key players back in the coming weeks, but several injured contributors may not return until after the bye. The Steelers will face a significant test as they manage those injuries and look to overcome their road struggles. The Steelers ruled out wide receiver Skowronek and cornerback Echols after both missed their first two practices of the week. JalenRamsey improved from a DNP on Wednesday to limited participation Thursday, while Watt also returned to limited work. Dowdle and Highsmith remained limited participants. Safety DeShon Elliott practiced fully for a second straight day, putting him in a promising position for a potential return from injured reserve. Heyward remained sidelined for rest, while Joseph-Day missed Wednesday’s practice with a triceps injury and was officially placed on injured reserve Thursday. Pittsburgh will look for further progress from its limited participants before Sunday’s matchup against the Saints in Paris. Pittsburgh has an opportunity to strengthen its position in the AFC North before heading into its bye week. However, both teams have plenty at stake as they navigate tight divisional races early in the season. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. away.headline: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game
away.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints continued preparations for Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Thursday, with starting right guard Cesar Ruiz remaining sidelined by a knee injury and kicker Daniel Carlson still absent for personal reasons. Ruiz, who sustained the injury during Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, did not participate in Thursday's practice after also missing Wednesday's session. His availability is a significant concern for a Saints offensive line preparing to face Pittsburgh's defensive front in Paris. Carlson also missed another practice after not traveling with the Saints to France. Instead, he awaits the arrival of his newborn child. Head coach Kellen Moore previously indicated that the kicker was expected to join the team before Sunday's game. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth remains a potential option if Carlson cannot return in time. The Saints added defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Thursday's report as a non-injury-related rest designation. He did not practice. There was encouraging news elsewhere on the injury report. Quarterback Tyler Shough continued to participate fully despite dealing with a left-hand injury. Backup quarterback Spencer Rattler, who was added to the report with a knee injury Thursday, also practiced fully. Running back C.J. Donaldson was upgraded to full participation after being limited Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry (head) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also practiced fully. Linebackers Anfernee Jennings (knee) and Kaden Elliss (calf) remained limited, as did running back Alvin Kamara, who is managing a back injury. Elliss' potential return would be particularly important as the linebacker has missed the previous three games while dealing with the calf injury. He has expressed optimism about playing against Pittsburgh. More clarity should come on Friday with the final injury report. The Week 7 game is apoears to be pivotal. Entering the bye week 3-4 and on a win streak versus 2-5 may the difference for New Orleans between making a push in the NFC South or a disappointing campaign. The Saints face the Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Central time in part of the NFL's international series. For the first time in a few weeks, they “lost” against the spread on Monday. The Niners are still 5-2 against the spread, with the NFL’s second-highest margin of victory at 11.2. They’re also tied for a league-high average margin of victory. So, when media members ask this: I would say the answer is no. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! The matchup against the Atlanta Falcons always looked like a scheduled loss, if there ever was one. The 49ers are 3-point road favorites, with the total on the game sitting at 49.5 on FanDuel Sportsbook . A high total and a low spread hint at a coin-flip game. We’ll see if Mike Evans plays. On the outside, it makes more sense to give Evans two weeks off so the Achilles soreness goes away and allows Evans to complete a game. But Kyle Shanahan seems to be putting the ball in Evans’s court. If the veteran feels healthy enough to play, he’ll play, even if the team knows they could lose him mid-game. There’s familiarity here, as Raheem Morris takes on his old team. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is one of the best in the league and worked with Shanahan in Atlanta a decade ago, not to mention as Morris’s defensive coordinator. Morris will need to find a way to limit Drake London, who has the 8th-highest target share among all NFL receivers. The Falcons throw it to London over 28% of the time. London is 11th in EPA per target. Not far behind London is his teammate Jahan Dotson, who is 14th in EPA per target. Tight end Kyle Pitts is fifth in EPA per target among tight ends. Atlanta is not short on weapons, and we haven’t even gotten to their biggest threat. Bijan Robinson is second in the NFL, averaging 5.77 yards per carry. He averages more yards after contact (4.64) than a good chunk of running backs do per carry. Robinson is a walking highlight who is heavily involved in Atlanta’s passing attack. Michael Penix is limited when it comes to being mobile, so that should work in the Niners favor. If there’s one person you’d want to attempt to slow down the Falcons, it’s the coach who drafted most of these players and watched them practice for the past few years: Raheem Morris. On the other side of the ball, no team has been better against the run than the Falcons defense. They’re first in EPA per rush and sixth in rushing success rate. Atlanta has allowed the third-fewest 10+ yard runs and is seventh in the percentage of runs they stuff. They make teams one-dimensional. This will be a Brock Purdy game. The Falcons won’t blitz Purdy nearly as often as Washington does, but they get pressure with four. That’s a big difference. Atlanta is fourth in pressure rate despite blitzing 23.7% of the time (26th in the NFL). You can throw on this defense. Atlanta is 20th and 21st in EPA per pass and passing success rate. Caleb Williams carved up the Dirty Birds for over 300 passing yards a week ago. A good chunk of those came in the first half. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had him a day. Tyler Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He threw for only 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw two touchdowns. Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He only threw for 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw for two touchdowns. Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers combined for 13 receptions for 115 yards. The week before, Tyler Shough threw the ball 48 times for 286 yards. Chris Olave had 116 yards. Of course, it’s far-fetched to imagine the Niners having a 100-yard receiver without Evans, but Shanahan has a full week to scheme up the non-Evans wideouts. A short road week with an early start on the East Coast, potentially without your leading receiver, against a team that has lost back-to-back games where they feel like they should have won. And the familiarity, paired with the weapons the Falcons have, makes this an intriguing game and a difficult schedule spot for a 6-0 team that could be feeling fat and happy a week away from the bye. away.headline: 49ers linked to Pro Bowl pass-rusher amid mounting injury issues
away.blurb: Bosa can return any week now, but the 49ers have been bracing to be without him for several weeks after he suffered a calf injury during warm-ups a few weeks ago. “Considering how important pressure is in the modern NFL, especially against the elite passers teams inevitably come up against in the playoffs, the Niners would be wise to bolster their edge-rushing unit with one of the best available free agents: Joey Bosa. The San Francisco 49ers may just be the best team in the NFL , but their mounting injury issues will catch up to them eventually. The team’s wide receiver corps has been ravaged in recent weeks with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Demarcus Robinson all going down with various ailments. The defensive side of the ball has also been hit hard by the injury bug as well. Defensive tackles Alfred Collins, CJ West, Sam Okuayinonu, edge-rushers Nick Bosa and Mikail Kamara, linebackers Nick Martin and Garret Wallow, cornerback Nate Hobbs, and safeties Marques Sigle and Darrick Forest are all either on injured reserve or have missed several weeks with their respective injuries. In the meantime, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes San Francisco should add to its pass-rush pool by signing a five-time Pro Bowler who’s quite familiar with one of the team’s top players. “While San Francisco features a top-five defense, it hasn’t generated pressure on a consistent basis,” Kay wrote . “An extended absence from top edge-rusher Nick Bosa — who has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 2 — has hindered the team’s ability to get after opposing quarterbacks. “… Even at the age of 31 with a history of injury, Joey Bosa can still be a force. He tallied five sacks, nine tackles for a loss, 16 quarterback hits and a league-leading five forced fumbles in 15 games with the Buffalo Bills last year and could be a key rotational piece for San Francisco in the back half of 2026.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported weeks ago that Joey Bosa was leaning toward retirement, but that doesn’t mean he can’t be tempted to play again in the right situation. Playing with his brother on a Super Bowl frontrunner where he won’t be relied on to play every down could be that perfect storm of temptation for him. away.headline: Why the 49ers Should Sit Out Mike Evans and Nick Bosa Against the Falcons
away.blurb: "So, we'll let these next couple of days play out and make a decision when we have to. Mike's that type of player that you wait, you let the process play itself out, and we'll see where we're at at the end of the week. Not fun—just kind of nagging," Lynch said of it. "And so, we're doing our best to kind of alleviate that from Mike so he can go play the fantastic football he has." In addition to Evans, Bosa could make a return for the first time since Week 2 after calf troubles. He didn't practice on Wednesday, but he may practice on Thursday ahead of the game. But even then, he should still miss the game. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/49ers/onsi as Why the 49ers Should Sit Out Mike Evans and Nick Bosa Against the Falcons . The San Francisco 49ers should rest Mike Evans and Nick Bosa against the Atlanta Falcons to avoid risking further injuries. It's almost Week 7 and San Francisco is 6-0 for the season. A perfect start to the season. But now it's time to think smartly about two key players who could feature against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Firstly, Evans is now dealing with Achilles tendinitis, with previous reports suggesting the issue will trouble him throughout the season . He's played in every game so far, despite dealing with rib issues and, more recently, Achilles soreness over the past three weeks. Yet he's continued to perform at an incredibly high level, and the 49ers are undoubtedly a stronger team with him on the field. But now it's time to rest him. The bye week is coming anyways, but general manager John Lynch isn't exactly sure whether he will play. "I wouldn't say 'not likely.' I think it's still TBD," Lynch said on his usual weekly appearance on Bay Area radio station KNBR. "We've got a couple of more days. We're going to take every bit of those to try to ascertain where Mike's at. He's done a really good job treating this thing, and obviously, we know of Mike's toughness. "He's kind of in that same Mike Evans bucket where we will kind of evaluate Nick here in the next couple of days, and I'm sure [head coach] Kyle [Shanahan] will have something for you on Friday while we're leaving for Atlanta," shared Lynch. In short, the bye week comes at a convenient time, so the 49ers should make the most of it by resting both players, even if they're cleared to play. Atlanta aren't the strongest opponents and San Francisco should be capable of winning regardless. Even if that means accepting a worst-case 6–1 record, having Bosa and Evans as healthy as possible heading into the bye is a bigger victory in the long run than risking further injuries for the sake of one game. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston (12) scores on a touchdown reception during the fourth quarter against New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens (21) at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published Oct 21, 2026 LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. away.headline: Cleveland Browns practice report for Thursday October 22 week 7
away.blurb: The good news is that four players were able to see more participation that Wednesday, as defensive tackle Maliek Collins (foot) went from limited participant to a full session. Safety Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) was listed as a limited participant after a DNP on Wednesday, which is the same status as center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee). Linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) also went from DNP to limited participation. Browns defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quadriceps) had his 21-day practice window opened on Oct. 6, and the time is ticking. He started the season on the reserve/injured list with a designation to return, but it doesn’t appear he’ll be able to go in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans. Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) did not practice for the second straight day, nor did offensive guard Teven Jenkins (back). The latter hurt himself Wednesday leading up to the Week 1 loss against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and he has missed all six games. Ten Players Listed as Limited Participants In addition to Delpit, Elgton Jenkins and Schwesinger working on a limited basis, defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle), wide receiver Denzel Boston (foot), wide receiver KC Concepcion (calf, quadriceps), defensive tackle Mason Graham (knee, ankle), offensive tackle Tytus Howard (knee), running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee) were limited. Collins, Gabriel and linebacker Justin Jefferson (hip) practiced in full. The Cleveland Browns have a total of 17 players listed with injuries on the practice report Thursday, and linebacker Quincy Williams joined the list due to a neck injury. That made four players who were unable to take part in the practice session. Kalia Davis Still Unable to Practice Quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back) also started the season on the reserve/injured list , and he had his practice window opened on Oct. 6, too. He has been able to practice in full the past two weeks, and it appears it is just a numbers game why he has yet to be tabbed for action. The team is already carrying starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, backup Shedeur Sanders and rookie Taylen Green. It remains to be seen how the team will handle the situation, and if, perhaps, one quarterback is moved before the NFL trade deadline. the practice report from today https://t.co/mviUaiwlz6 Judkins missed the Week 6 game against the Baltimore Ravens, so former practice report additions Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime each saw meaningful roles in the 13-10 win over the Ravens, with Estime scoring a touchdown. That would be the same setup again in Week 7 if Judkins is inactive, Sampson was hurt in Week 1, and he remains on the IR .

away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: What Robert Saleh said about Jordan Elliott situation, response from Titans and NFL
home.blurb: "The (defensive line) room is really close," Saleh said. "For JFM to go out there and kind of help Jordan through with whatever he was dealing with at that moment I thought was really admirable on JFM’s part." The incident, which is under review by the NFL, followed a practice altercation with teammate JC Latham. Teammate John Franklin-Myers was credited with de-escalating the situation before it worsened. Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Oct. 21 that Jordan Elliott pulled a gun in the team facility's parking lot after a practice altercation last week, leading to the defensive tackle's release this week. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. Saleh praised the organization and the NFL's response to the incident, citing a "pause" by the team and the league in getting Elliott assistance for what Saleh called a sign for "a cry for help" instead of involving law enforcement. "And the reason why I think the NFL and the organization did an outstanding job is because this is a man who is father, a great husband. He’s never committed a crime in his entire life," Saleh said. "And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. And the first question that I think everyone forgets to ask is why would a great man, a great father, a man who shows up on time every day, works his ass off every day, contributes the way he's supposed to contribute, is well-liked in the locker room — Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? "And to me, those are small signs of a cry of help. In terms of, obviously there’s something greater happening. And I thought the team and the NFL did an outstanding job with regards to pausing and asking those questions and checking every single box with regards to getting him the help that he needs." Saleh vouched for Elliott's character despite the incident. The veteran defensive tackle with seven seasons in the NFL played for Saleh in San Francisco last year before joining the Titans in free agency in the spring. "These kids go through a lot. A lot. And... I will stand on the table for Jordan’s character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property. And sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a helluva run-stopping defensive tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act." What happened with Jordan Elliott at the Titans' facility? Elliott attempted to retrieve a gun from his vehicle after a practice altercation with JC Latham on Oct. 15, according to multiple reports. home.headline: Tennessee Titans' Alontae Taylor responds to surprise benching
home.blurb: Tennessee invested heavily in Taylor and projected him as a full-time outside cornerback in the new system, a role he'd take on for the first extended period of his NFL career. That transition hasn't gone smoothly so far, and it appears the “reset” head coach Robert Saleh talks about may include a return to a nickel role. Taylor is clearly frustrated by the decision, though he said he wouldn’t change his decision to join the Titans organization and will keep showing up and doing everything he can to get back in the lineup, while hinting at a possible return to the slot. “Yeah, I was told that I would come here to play corner. Um, and that’s what my mentality was. Um, but now, um, things are changing, and I’ll just adapt," he said, while also pointing out the scheme is “different than anything I’ve played.” Amid talk about Jordan Elliott on Wednesday at the Tennessee Titans facility, cornerback Alontae Taylor sat down to discuss his unexpected inactive-day listing for Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. Yes, the move would frustrate the Tennessee native, who is now playing for the Titans, but in the long term, it could be the best thing for both Taylor and the Titans. Taylor is a tremendous nickel cornerback, and that role is essential in every NFL defense; those players are hard to find. Time will tell if it was the right decision for Taylor and the organization. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. away.headline: Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren still out on Colts injury report; rookie added
away.blurb: A new addition to the Week 7 injury report is LB CJ Allen with an ankle injury. He was listed as limited on Thursday. Allen's role as a rookie has been relatively small. As the backup MIKE linebacker, he has not rotated in often at the WILL position. Justin Walley (knee) was limited on Thursday after being a non-participant on Day 1. Jaylon Carlies (ribs) was a full participant for the second consecutive day, while Ashton Dulin (hamstring) was again limited. Both have missed the last two games. Anthony Gould (concussion) did not practice again. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren still out on Colts injury report; rookie added Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Rigoberto Sanchez all remain sidelined on the Indianapolis Colts ' second Week 7 injury report. Gardner is working through a calf injury he suffered in Sunday's loss to Tennessee. Gardner is reportedly considered week-to-week with this injury. Warren continues to work through a groin injury he sustained last Friday. He did not play against the Titans. Sanchez sustained a foot injury on Sunday during the blocked punt. Veteran punter Thomas Morstead was signed to the practice squad this week. Some good news for the Colts is that Bryce Boettcher (groin), Matt Goncalves (ankle), Drew Ogletree (ankle), Jerry Tillery (personal), and Jalen Travis (foot) were all upgraded to full participants. Jonathan Taylor, Charvarius Ward, and Keenan Allen all returned from rest days, while Grover Stewart took his vet rest day on Thursday.

away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . Gardner left the game during Tennessee’s opening possession of the second half after experiencing discomfort in his left leg. According to ESPN’s Stephen Holder, Gardner requested to leave the field before trainers began examining his left calf. Gardner entered Sunday’s matchup having appeared in all six games this season. According to Colts Wire, opposing quarterbacks had completed nine of 17 passes targeting Gardner for 195 yards, while the veteran cornerback recorded three pass breakups. His ability to match up against opposing receivers makes him an important part of Indianapolis’ defensive strategy. Losing Gardner for an extended period could force the Colts to make significant adjustments in coverage, particularly against teams featuring explosive passing attacks. However, the immediate concern is determining the severity of his latest injury. He has compiled 178 receptions for 2,302 yards (12.9 avg.) and 16 touchdowns. Hardman Jr. has tallied 26 carries for 190 yards (7.3 avg.) and three touchdowns. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium against the New York Jets (2-4). For New York, Sunday offers an opportunity to take another step big picture as an organization and in the moment remain on the fringe of the playoff picture. The Jets are certainly far more competitive than they were a season ago but after a loss last weekend to the Patriots and looking at the rest of their schedule, a win Sunday at home against the winless Dolphins is paramount. They will need more from their offense, though, if they are to win as the Jets average just 18.7 points per game. Miami’s offense is scoring an average of 14 points per game but it’s worse than that for the winless Dolphins. Miami has yet to even lead for even a second in any of their five games this season. New York enters the game following a 26-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 6. The Jets fell behind early and could not overcome their mistakes despite another competitive defensive effort. Prior to that defeat, they snapped a four-game losing streak with a 17-12 win over Cleveland, showing the formula they hope to replicate against Miami: strong defense, ball control, and avoiding turnovers. The Dolphins’ most recent outing was a 31-24 loss to Cincinnati on October 11, arguably their most encouraging offensive performance of the season. Miami rallied in the second half and scored 24 points after managing only 46 total points across its previous four games, but defensive breakdowns once again proved costly as the losing streak extended to five games. Quarterback play will be one of the game’s biggest storylines. Veteran Geno Smith has provided stability for the Jets, throwing for 1,336 yards with seven touchdowns and just one interception through six games. While the Jets’ offense has not consistently produced explosive numbers, Smith has protected the football and given New York a chance to win most weeks. Not the same situation in South Beach. Miami’s Malik Willis has been underwhelming. Yes, the skill positions are lacking with the Dolphins, but the long-time Green Bay backup has to be better. Willis has thrown for 849 yards with a mere two touchdowns along with four interceptions. The Dolphins need greater efficiency if they are going to win or even lead a game. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was treated for an injured thumb on his right, throwing hand, but he fully practiced four days before a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . Willis did not throw at a bye week Monday practice that was open to reporters. Willis did not mention the thumb injury when he met with reporters a short time before the first Jets injury report of the week was released. "(Coach Jeff Hafley) just wanted to get us a little rest, and he wanted to get some young guys in there and see how they were progressing through this season," Willis said when asked what he was dealing with. "But, pretty good." Hafley said at the start of the week that Willis would be fine. "He should be good," Hafley said. "I mean, was he dealing with something? Yeah, I mean, we had a bunch of guys after the (Cincinnati) game that were having a Tuesday practice; usually we don't go until Wednesday. So just rested him on that, but I foresee him being good to go." Miami Dolphins injury report includes Malik Willis thumb Willis has said he hasn't been good enough in his first five Dolphins starts. He is 29th in the NFL with a passer rating of 68.4. He has 2 passing touchdowns, 2 rushing touchdowns, 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles. Willis said he balanced football review and rest and recovery during the bye week. What does Willis think about outside of football? "I mean, the Lord, bro," Willis said. "I keep waking up every day. I got an opportunity to come in here and do my job. I have a family that loves me. I have more than enough. I make it to work safe every day, bro. It's a dangerous world. And we just overlook all these things that are blessings. I try not to do that. And at the same time, I hold myself to the highest of standards. And I just try to focus on the process. home.headline: Jets finally get some good Breece Hall injury news on Week 7 practice report
home.blurb: One of the biggest is the Breece Hall quad injury, which has kept him out for multiple weeks now. However, the Jets got some good news before Week 7 on Hall's injury. As the Jets announced in their Thursday Week 7 practice injury report, the star running back was finally upgraded at practice, as he was no longer a DNP but instead listed as a "limited" participant. The Jets shared their Week 7 injury report for their game against the Miami Dolphins . Right in the middle of the injury report, Hall was seen with his quad injury as going from a "DNP" on Wednesday to a "LP" on Thursday. What that means is that, for the first time in a while, Hall got in a limited practice, which bodes well for his chances of suiting up on Sunday against the AFC East rival Dolphins. He isn't guaranteed to play this week, but getting in a limited practice, going from not participating on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday, is a sign that he's trending in the right direction. Jets fans should keep a very close eye on the Friday injury report, because if Hall's a full participant, he's as good as playing. But even another limited participation would indicate his work Thursday went well, and he'd have a chance to go in Week 7.
