home.headline: New York Jets get Adonai Mitchell, Dylan Parham back at practice
home.blurb: Despite a social media tease by running back Breece Hall, he did not practice on Wednesday, raising doubts as to whether he will be available on Sunday. Hall had used the word “Soon” on Instagram earlier this week, sparking chatter that he was close to getting back from a quad injury. Running back Braelon Allen has filled in admirably for Hall and could be used in a dual backfield when Hall is fully healthy. Returning to practice was the long-absent receiver Adonai Mitchell, who has been out since the earth cooled with a finger injury. Mystery still surrounds the exact nature of Mitchell’s injury, which required an unspecified “procedure” after the Jets denied he needed surgery. They now say his return is a matter of pain management. If he is indeed back and can play, his return would mark the first time since opening day that the Jets have core receivers Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and Mitchell available at the same time. Also back at practice was left guard Dylan Parham, who was playing well for the Jets when he went down with a knee injury. How mobile he’ll be is a matter to be determined, but he would be a key addition. The Jets offensive line has struggled in his absence and could use a boost from his return. The Jets defense is another matter. Edge Joseph Ossai and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa did not practice on Wednesday and remain week-to-week. Ossai has been battling an ankle injury, while Mauigoa has a quad injury after being shelved with a back injury. Edge Will McDonald IV was listed on Wednesday’s injury report as limited by a toe injury, while defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat was limited with an elbow issue. Barring a setback, both are anticipated to play against Miami, although Thursday’s practice will be crucial for both. The New York Jets have a long list of ifs, maybes, and might as far as who will play this weekend against the Miami Dolphins. The Jets are trying to find a rhythm with a defense that has been hot and cold this season. The Jets followed an 8-sack game against the Cleveland Browns with 0 sacks against the New England Patriots. Miami has had pass protection problems, which would make for an ideal situation for edge David Bailey, who has five sacks and numerous pressures on the season.

Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. So, can they extend the run to three against their division rivals? Carolina had been getting dominated by Tampa for a long time, losing nine of 10 matchups going into last season. But the Panthers finally stopped the bleeding with a 23-20 win at home in December. The Buccaneers got them back, though—winning the regular season finale in Tampa 16-14. For Sunday's bout, Pete Prisco at CBS Sports sees a nail-biter—and predicts the Panthers to come out with a one-point victory. Prisco writes: The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 With the status of Mayfield still up in the air, the Bucs—per head coach Todd Bowles— are operating as if undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will get the start at quarterback. Daniels got Tampa their first win of the season against Dallas a couple of weeks ago. However, he's 1-2 on the year, and his numbers are not that impressive. In four starts, he's completed 61.2 percent of his passes—totaling 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions. His 63.3 passer rating ranks 33rd in the league while his 45.0 quarterback rating ranks 23rd. As far as Carolina's quarterback goes, Young has entered the week as the NFL's leader in passing yards per game. Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Injuries threw Panthers rookie CB Will Lee III into deep end. Now, he's just 'trying to eat'
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles put that moniker to the test Sunday, when Lee often matched up against DeVonta Smith, a 2021 top-10 pick and Heisman Trophy winner out of Alabama. Though Smith caught a touchdown against Lee in the fourth quarter of Carolina's 25-14 win, the 2026 fourth-round pick finished with six tackles and three pass breakups, becoming the first Carolina rookie with three passes defensed in a game since Keith Taylor in 2021. "It was a great matchup. He's a great receiver, Heisman winner, wide receiver one over there in Philly. And he's a great guy to compete against," Lee said. "That's my big thing. I love competing. I don't care who it is out there, I'm gonna go out there and give it my all." "Talk about Will Lee and the way that he was challenging their best receiver or whoever they put out in front. He got some penalties called on him, but he was in the mix, and he was right there at the top of coverage," Canales said. "He could be a little cleaner with his hands, but I'm not going to back Will Lee off of playing that style of football. I thought that was excellent." The 6-1, 195-pound Lee was known for his strong man coverage skills at Kansas State, where he played in 2023, and Texas A&M, where he spent his final two college seasons. He developed a reputation for being physical and handsy at both stops, not unlike the scouting report on Horn after the Panthers drafted him with the No. 8 pick out of South Carolina in 2021. "I'm a juco guy. I'm grimy. I like to play physical. It's all love at the end of the day, but I'm a competitive person," he said. "I feel like you're out there to embarrass me, and I'm out there to stop you from doing what you're supposed to do. I'm trying to eat, so that's my goal." "He said it's just like repetition. You've gotta learn and feel out the game when you're out there. Some refs are gonna call it different than others, and you've just gotta play the game," Lee said. "He just said be confident in yourself out there and your technique, and you're gonna be just fine." "His demeanor is that of a veteran," Scott said. "A lot of times when you're out there as a young guy, you might have to keep them from being up and down with the result of the drive or the play, giving up a big catch or getting a PBU. They kind of ride that wave. But Will, for the most part, is pretty steady, which definitely makes it easier on everybody." Injuries threw Panthers rookie CB Will Lee III into deep end. home.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. Cleveland is now ahead of the Ravens in the division, and Baltimore wants to avoid a similar fate in Week 7 against Cincinnati. While the Ravens have won three of the last four games Huntley has started in place of Jackson, they are still just 7-12 without the star quarterback all time. It's unlikely that the Ravens would close as favorites, even at home, if Jackson were to miss the game against Joe Burrow and Co. in Week 7. This season, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. The Ravens star leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Baltimore's practice reports should give a better look into Jackson's status this week, but bettors should treat him as highly questionable until he is able to return to the practice field. His desire to have a big game against his former team is already on full display, as starting Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson has called for Hendrickson to get multiple sacks on Sunday. "I believe that this game for him is about to be one of those one's, like multiple sack games, I'm calling it," Simpson said. Immediately, a scuffle broke out between the two on Brown's first snap of training camp with the Bengals. He acknowledged his respect for Hendrickson and how his past practices with him should help him this Sunday. "That's who he is, That's why I respect him, He's a fighter," Brown said. I can't put my finger on that, But at the end of the day, I've got to play Sunday." Hendrickson consistently dominated opposing linemen with the Bengals, and he has continued to do so with the Ravens. Over six weeks, he ranks third in the NFL in pressure rate per Next Gen Stats, with a 30% pass-rush win rate across 73 plays. Brown pointed to Hendrickson's passion to remain a dominant force on the defensive line as the reason the Bengals signed him in 2021 and the Ravens signed him this offseason. He also said Hendrickson will remain one of his good friends whenever he retires. "A lot of passion, that's why they paid him there, that's why we paid him here," Brown said. "That's why he's been so successful. I have no friends with D-linemen not on my team. When I retire, one day, Trey will be one of my good friends." As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. Joe Burrow looking forward to facing Trey Hendrickson Burrow has practiced against Hendrickson many a time over the years, but the two have never been opponents in a real game before. There's no confusion on what he's expecting from No. 91, now in purple instead of orange. "It'll be fun, it'll be fun," Burrow said of seeing Hendrickson rushing at him . away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was able to get some "limited" work in at practice on Wednesday, but the betting market seems to think that the two-time MVP will miss Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. Lamar Jackson Injury Update Completely Flips Bengals vs. Ravens Odds for NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. B

Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. home.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson inches one step closer toward injury return
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens are sure hoping superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson can return after he missed the past two games with an ankle injury. Jackson returned to practice in limited form on Wednesday, and there were still plenty of questions about whether or not he could go against the Cincinnati Bengals. On Thursday, the Ravens released another injury report, and Jackson was listed as "limited" for the second straight day, which bodes well with regard to his chances of playing against the Ravens' AFC North foe. Jackson reportedly "moved around well" during the practice session that was open to the media. Jackson suffered the injury in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, and Tyler "Snoop" Huntley has been filling in under center for Baltimore. Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons, and he threw for two touchdowns while rushing for another. In Week 6, the Ravens fell to the Cleveland Browns, 13-10, on the road, and Huntley went just 19-of-31 for 165 yards with a score. The Ravens are 4-2 and the Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers are also 4-2. The Bengals are 3-2, so the AFC North is very crowded with one-third of the season in the rearview mirror. Jackson has a chance to play on Sunday, and his final status should be revealed this weekend. Want more articles like this? Follow Yardbarker on MSN to see more of our exclusive NFL content. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. picks.headline: Does J.J. McCarthy give the Giants worse odds against the Texans?
picks.blurb: Does J.J. McCarthy give the Giants worse odds against the Texans? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Does J.J. McCarthy give the Giants worse odds against the Texans? New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy runs with the ball against the New Orleans Saints. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Chris Pflum Thu, October 22, 2026 at 5:09 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads We already knew that the New York Giants were going to be underdogs going into their Week 7 match against the Houston Texans. The line has moved significantly by Thursday, dropping the Giants to 10.5-point underdogs against the Texans, per Fanduel . The Texans have consistently been viewed as being better than their record despite their 0-4 start to the season. The Giants, meanwhile, have been viewed with skepticism despite their 3-1 start. So it was expected that the Giants would be underdogs when this week's opening odds came out. The Giants' odds have been dropping all week, and they were 9.5-point underdogs by Wednesday. It's notable that the Giants' odds got longer the day after they made a quarterback change, dropping a full point despite J.J. McCarthy coming off a game in which he threw for nearly 250 yards and a touchdown in less than a quarter. The change in the odds is likely due to a combination of factors. The Texans are getting explosive playmaker Tank Dell back from an injury that cost him the 2025 season, while the Giants could be without multiple starters in their secondary. The Giants are also dealing with injuries along their offensive line while still searching for an answer for how to run the ball. That said, the change does seem to reflect the fact that there just isn't much confidence in J.J. McCarthy. He's an undeniable draft bust for the Vikings and he'll be going against a defense that was the class of the NFL the last time DeMeco Ryans was running it. Whatever the reason, or reasons, the Giants are facing long odds on what could be a very consequential game before their bye week. A win going into their bye (with the Eagles and Commanders looming after the BYE) would mean that the team will maintain their 1.5-game advantage in the division and have a better-than-even chance of making the playoffs. However, a loss will shrink that lead down to just half a game and make it significantly less likely that they make the playoffs. The Giants could certainly use the upset win, but that seems to be increasingly less likely.

picks.headline: Giants’ John Harbaugh makes J.J. McCarthy vs. Jameis Winston pick for Week 7 vs. Texans
picks.blurb: Giants’ John Harbaugh makes J.J. McCarthy vs. Jameis Winston pick for Week 7 vs. Texans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Malik Brown, ClutchPoints Wed, October 21, 2026 at 5:21 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants will be facing the Houston Texans in Week 7, and many have been wondering who the starting quarterback will be. J.J. McCarthy came into the game last week during the second half and almost led the team to victory, and that may have been enough for head coach John Harbaugh to give him the start. It was indeed enough, as McCarthy is set to be QB1 , according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "Source: The Giants plan to start J.J. McCarthy on Sunday vs. Houston," Fowler wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It felt like a no-brainer for the Giants, especially with how Jameis Winston had played over the past few weeks. Yes, he led them to some wins, but the last two weeks were not great. Against the Washington Commanders, they ended the game in a tie, and against the New Orleans Saints, he was benched for his play. That's when McCarthy came in and lit up the Saints in the fourth quarter, and he finished with 243 passing yards, one touchdown and an interception. Following the game, Winston was asked about his chances of being the starter for Week 7. "That's him, that's a decision that he'll have to make. What I would love is to just put myself in a better position to execute, and that just starts with me, things I can control," Winston said. It looks like Harbaugh has gone with the hot hand, and there was always a chance that McCarthy would find some playing time this season. After some rough years with the Minnesota Vikings, the hope is that McCarthy can find new life with the Giants this season and maybe build up his resume so other teams may be interested in him next season. away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. home.blurb: The Houston Texans finally had a reason to celebrate after Ka'imi Fairbairn's last-second field goal sealed a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. But the victory also came with concerns for a defense that had struggled to meet expectations this season. Safety Reed Blankenship left the game with a concussion, and coach DeMeco Ryans gave an update on his condition ahead of Sunday's matchup against the New York Giants. Another starting safety, Jalen Pitre, also remained uncertain to return as Houston prepared for Week 7. Blankenship had to clear the NFL's concussion protocol when Ryans spoke to reporters on Tuesday, October 21. The safety suffered the injury in the second quarter against Jacksonville while attempting to tackle running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. He could not return to the game, leaving Houston to prepare for its next matchup without knowing whether he would be available. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. away.headline: Broncos injury report: Pat Surtain, Jonah Coleman, Talanoa Hufanga, Jonah Elliss updates
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: First, the good news following the portion of Thursday's practice open to media members: cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ), running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ) and cornerback Riley Moss ( ribs ) continue to practice. Surtain might be more likely to make his game-day return in Week 8 , but getting practice reps is a step in the right direction. Jahdae Barron has been starting in place of PS2, and Taylor Rapp did a nice job helping replace Hufanga last week. Meanwhile, Coleman and outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper ( reinstated ) are both candidates to return to the 53-man roster later this week. There's mixed news on the injury front as the Denver Broncos continue preparing for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals . Now, the bad news: safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) remain sidelined. Hufanga is expected to miss at least one more game , and coach Sean Payton seemingly hinted after Wednesday's practice that Elliss could land on short-term injured reserve later this week. Denver's scheduled to practice again on Friday before releasing a final injury report with game statuses for Sunday's showdown with the Cardinals . All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. NFL Week 7 Spread Picks All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Patriots vs. Bears Spread Pick The Bears team is a completely different squad with Caleb Williams back on the field. The Chicago defense has also been much better this season than people give it credit for. Pick: Bears -3 (-102) Steelers vs. Saints The Saints have the worst run defense in the NFL, and now they have to take on a strong Pittsburgh run game. Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry this season, so he should carry the Steelers to a win in France. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (-102) 49ers vs. Falcons The Falcons' secondary is banged up, and now they have to take on an MVP candidate in Brock Purdy. San Francisco's offense should be able to score at will in this game. Pick: 49ers -3 (-102) Browns vs. Titans The Browns are just a better version of the Titans. They have a slightly better quarterback and a stronger defense. The only world I'd ever bet on the Titans this season is when they're getting more than a field goal's worth of points. Pick: Browns -1.5 (-110) Colts vs. Vikings The Vikings' defense is going to put the Colts' offense in a blender. They're the best run defense in the NFL, and their ability to blitz is going to confuse Daniel Jones. As long as the Vikings' offense can score enough in this game, they should win comfortably. Pick: Vikings -6.5 (-108) Dolphins vs. Jets The Dolphins have had one of the most difficult schedules in the NFL to begin this season. This is by far their easiest opponent yet, so maybe the Dolphins will be able to put up a fight. Pick: Dolphins +4.5 (-105) Buccaneers vs. Panthers The rule with any NFC South team is: the moment you think they're good, bet against them. Let's also not forget that the Buccaneers' defense has quietly been one of the better units in the NFL this season. They can keep them in this game. Pick: Buccaneers +3 (+100) Bengals vs. Ravens Lamar Jackson is likely out for one more game, which is bad news for the Ravens as they now have to take on a Bengals team that's fresh off a BYE and has been playing some solid football on both offense and defense. McCarthy, so I think this is going to be an ugly game for the Giants. Pick: Texans -10.5 (-108) Broncos vs. Cardinals No team has had a tougher schedule so far this season than the Denver Broncos. Now, they get to take on a Cardinals team that ranks dead last in the NFL in net yards per play. I'm surprised this spread is set at such a low number. Pick: Broncos -4.5 (-110) Packers vs. Lions The Lions are coming off a BYE and they get Brian Branch back in their secondary, which is going to give their defense a massive boost moving forward. Now is the time to buy some stock in the Lions. Pick: Lions -3 (-110) Rams vs. Raiders The Rams' injuries may be piling up, but they should still be bigger favorites against the Raiders, who are far worse than their record indicates. Their defense has become a bottom-10 unit, and they can't run the football. The moment Kirk Cousins begins to regress, things are going to get ugly in Las Vegas. "They're playing really good football right now," Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Packers. "Two of their best games have been these back-to-back games. Plus-six in the turnover ratio the last two weeks; it was seven takeaways on defense, man. It's an opportunistic defense. They fly around the football. They disguise well and create issues. […] it's been an outstanding test for us. Hell of an opponent, first division game of the season at home. We're looking forward to it, but this is a real good team right now playing good football." Let's take a closer look at the Packers' coaching staff, the scheme they run, and scouting notes from their most recently viewed games. Packer s head coach: Matt LaFleur NFL coaching seasons: 18th (Texans, Washington, Falcons, Rams, Titans, Packers) Head coaching seasons : 8th (Packers 2019-present) Offensive coordinator : 2nd (Rams 2017, Titans 2018) Other coaching roles held : QB coach, Offensive assistant Influences: Mike Shanahan, Kyle Shanahan, and Sean McVay Coached under: Both Shanahans, McVay, Gary Kubiak, Dan Quinn, Mike Vrabel Play caller : Yes Dan Campbell on LaFleur: "Matt's (LaFleur) doing a hell of a job. They have. They've gotten better every week. […] what Matt's done over there and they've done offensively, they've evolved in areas, but there are some things that they're going to hang their hat on. They're good at and they're not going to change that. They'll just wrinkle it, man, a bunch of eye candy to try to get you off of it. And it's effective. It's still effective. It's been effective every year." Offensive coordinato r: Adam Stenavich NFL coaching seasons : 10th (49ers, Packers) Offensive coordinator seasons : 5th (Packers 2022-present) Previous coaching positions : Run game coordinator, OL coach, Assistant OL coach Playing career : 5 seasons on NFL practice squads (Panthers, Packers, Cowboys, Texans) Influences: Kyle Shanahan and Matt LaFleur Coached under: Shanahan and LaFleur Offensive scheme Passing game : West Coast Shanahan offense Running scheme : Wide zone/Shanahan system, introduced more gap/trap/wham concepts Scouting notes : Core concepts of LaFleur's scheme: Early down play-action, pre-snap motion, bunch formations, spread the ball around, vertical attack, explosives, screens, chip blocks are used to slow the pass rush, adaptability Primarily utilize 11-personnel: 60% of the time — 12-personnel: 25%; 13-personnel: 15% Efficient passing attack — 269.3 passing yards per game (5th) Have moved the ball well; struggled to score touchdowns early in the season, but have improved Pass yards per play: 7.5 (12th); EPA per pass: 0.05 (13th) Red zone touchdown efficiency: 50% (22nd); Jordan Love EPA in red zone: -0.24 (32nd) Deep ball is the strength of this offense, but also situational, as it is more frequently used when they have the lead (15.5%), but is not as prevalent when trailing (6.67%) — per Anthony Balaj's film study 3rd most explosive passing plays in the NFL The deep ball also leads to big penalties; gained 135 yards on penalties on deep passes through six games Majority of all targets go to top three skill players: WR Matthew Golden, WR Christian Watson, TE Tucker Kraft Target share: Golden 26%, Watson 22%, Kraft 17% — That's two-thirds of the passes thrown by Love Offensive line play has been an issue, both in the pass and run game Pressures allowed: 97 (29th); pressure rate: 40.2% (25th); quick pressure rate 22.1% (22nd) Time to pressure: 2.36 seconds (32nd) Jordan Love EPA when pressured: -0.26 (17th), per Sumer Sports Run game has been, by far, the worst rushing attack in the NFL Rushing yards per game: 59.8 (32nd); per carry: 2.9 (32nd); Rush EPA: -0.29 (32nd); success rate: 30.4% (32nd, per NextGenStats, via NFLPro); DVOA stuffed runs: 25% (32nd) OL stats: PFF blocking grade: 47.3 (32nd); DVOA (32); adjusted yards (32nd) RB Josh Jacobs is eligible to return, and while the Packers are playing coy, the Lions say they expect him to play — but how ready will he be after not playing football for the last month and a half? Dan Campbell on Packers offense: "They've settled some things in in that old line. […] (QB Jordan) Love, man. He makes it go. He is the secret sauce. Every team in the division finished with a winning record in 2025, and that trend has continued into this year . Now the Packers and Lions are gearing up for a huge divisional matchup that could have huge ramifications come playoff time. Green Bay is looking strong after a questionable start to the season. They are on a three-game winning streak after taking care of Dallas on Sunday Night Football . The Packers are still a bit behind the Vikings, but getting a win in Week 7 will get them one step closer to catching up. Meanwhile, Detroit quieted their doubters in Week 5 after crushing Arizona in the desert. The Lions even got a solid game from their defense, something that has eluded them for most of the season. But Detroit is coming off their bye week, so it is impossible to know if they'll carry over that momentum or come out flat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Which team will come out on top in this massive divisional matchup? Here are three bold predictions before the NFC North clash between the Lions and Packers in Week 7. Jared Goff throws his first interception of the season, but still shreds Packers defense Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Goff may be the most underrated quarterback in the entire NFL this season. He may look like a quarterback from a different age, but Goff can still sling it with the best of them. Detroit's franchise quarterback has 1,485 passing yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. That's right, he still has not thrown an interception at any point this season. This speaks to how careful Goff is with the football, no doubt owing to his veteran experience. All of that said, this could be the week that the streak comes to an end. The Lions should not underestimate the Packers' defensive unit, even if they don't have Micah Parsons in Week 7. Green Bay has one of the better coverage units in the NFL this season despite an unproven cornerback room. Even more impressive is that they lead the NFL in interceptions with nine through the first six games. If any team is going to snap Goff's streak, it will be the packers. Goff will throw his first interception of the season against Green Bay on Sunday. All good things must come to an end, including his impressive streak of clean games. However, that doesn't mean he'll wilt against the Packers. Detroit will finish this game with at least 400 passing yards, shredding Green Bay's secondary from wire to wire. Josh Jacobs rumbles for 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns in 2026 debut Green Bay's one weakness this season has been their rushing attack. The Packers are averaging a pitiful 59.8 rushing yards per game this season. That is due to a combination of offensive line issues and a thin running back group. But the latter is about to change. Josh Jacobs looks slated to return in Week 7 after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. "I would say Jacobs has been preliminarily cleared and is expected to play this week. He is going to practice. He's going to be on the field. They say he has kept in good shape, and the Green Bay Packers, who have had a really solid start to the season, probably could use a little bit of an improved running game, and they get Josh Jacobs in Week 7 to come in and do it," NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Wednesday via Good Morning Football. Getting Jacobs back won't fix everything overnight. After all, it is fair to be skeptical of how ready he truly is after staying away from football for over a month. Still, Jacobs could have a breakout game against Detroit if Matt LaFleur dials up enough carries for him. Jacobs will go over 100 rushing yards and score two touchdowns against the Lions. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images Of course, the matchup that everyone will be watching in this one is Jordan Love against Detroit's struggling secondary. Green Bay suddenly looks capable of keeping up with Detroit's offense. The emergence of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden has unlocked the team's passing attack. On paper, they're in the same tier as Detroit in terms of passing yards per game. The good news for the Lions is that Brian Branch is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Packers in Week 7. It is impossible to know just how good Branch will look after last season's Achilles injury . Getting him back is also no guarantee that Detroit's defense will magically play better. But it is a start. In the long term, getting Branch back should do wonders for the Lions. Unfortunately, it won't be enough to win this game. The Packers win by one score in an epic shootout at Ford Field. Related: Caleb Williams and Drake Maye are on fire. Can either defense make a stand in Bears-Patriots? away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ latest injury update might have determined that a former high draft pick won’t play another snap for the team. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was asked on Thursday whether tight end Luke Musgrave will play again this season as he recovers from a neck injury . LaFleur’s answer didn’t offer much clarity about a 2026 return. At that point, the Packers said Musgrave could potentially return at some point during the season. Since then, his situation hasn’t become any clearer. Based on LaFleur’s comments, it doesn’t sound promising for the former second-round pick. Tight end Luke Musgrave remains sidelined with a neck injury, and head coach Matt LaFleur was asked Thursday about his outlook for the rest of 2026. “That’s tough to say right now," LaFleur said. "Until proven otherwise, I would say no, but I would never close the door on that." That isn’t the tone of a team expecting its tight end back anytime soon. And with Musgrave in the final year of his rookie contract, the timing makes his situation even more significant. A long road back from the neck injury Musgrave suffered the neck injury during the offseason program and opened training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Green Bay then moved him to the reserve/PUP list to start the regular season , which forced him to miss at least four games. The expectation, though, was that he would eventually miss much more than that. From Day 1 starter to afterthought Green Bay selected Musgrave in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft, and he immediately took over as the starting tight end. However, he suffered a lacerated kidney in Week 11 of his rookie season, and he never was the full-time starter again for the Packers. Part of that came from Tucker Kraft taking the position by storm. But more than that, Musgrave never developed as a blocker or as a YAC player. He is a solid receiver, but he never materialized into what the front office expected when it drafted him. Because LaFleur’s offensive structure demands blocking from tight ends, Musgrave gradually became an afterthought on the depth chart. In his three seasons with the Packers so far, Musgrave played 35 games with 22 starts. He totaled 65 receptions, 649 yards, and just one regular season touchdown. He also appeared in four playoff games, catching seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown. That score came as a rookie against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, Musgrave is in the final year of his rookie deal, and it’s unclear whether he will stay in Green Bay beyond this season. More likely than not, he won’t. Therefore, if Musgrave misses the rest of the year, he has potentially already played his final snap as a Packer. The Packers somewhat rebuilt the tight end room right before the regular season. picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. picks.headline: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams
picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home.
