Garrett would be out at least four weeks. Myles Garrett's Return Timeline Raises More Questions While Garrett recovered from arthroscopic knee surgery, reports flooded in on his potential return timeline. To be fair, the Rams never put a timeline on Garrett. However, according to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport on September 27, Garrett was given a six-week timeline . Rapoport reported then that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline. On October 4, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added more information . Jones noted that the six-week timeline would be a worst-case scenario. Fantasy managers see a roster problem when a player goes down, but Matthew Stafford sees a teammate robbed of the work he put in. The Los Angeles Rams quarterback addressed his team’s injury list on Oct. 21. Head coach Sean McVay expects wide receiver Davante Adams to sit six to 10 weeks with an injured hamstring. Stafford, the reigning NFL MVP, said fan reactions miss the real loss. Los Angeles fell to 2-4 with an 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18, its second straight defeat. Defensive lineman Poona Ford ruptured his triceps in that game and is done for the year. Fellow lineman Kobie Turner, who strained his groin, went to injured reserve. McVay said Oct. 19 that linebacker Nate Landman is going through the concussion protocol. Edge rusher Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson are still on IR. In his 18th NFL season, Stafford has 11 touchdown passes and six interceptions. He sees this slide as a leadership test. “That’s when my role becomes even more important as a leader, as somebody that can try and help steady the ship for us,” he said. The Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25, then face the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders , and Cardinals before their bye.

away.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
away.blurb: “Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what’s the best way is to move the ball and score points,” McVay said. “Because of some of the situations that we’ve been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it’s an excuse. I’d like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that’s reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives.” There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It’s a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They’re unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let’s take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. Let's take a look at everyone's upset pick for Week 7. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Mike Kadlick , NFL Senior News Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 7 Upset Pick Atlanta Falcons (+136) vs. San Francisco 49ers The undefeated 49ers could be headed toward a trap game in Atlanta with Mike Evans dealing with an Achilles injury. Brock Purdy and his offense struggled without Evans during the second half of Monday night’s win against the Commanders. They nearly blew a 20-point advantage due to their inability to gain first downs and kill the clock. To make matters worse, Deebo Samuel Sr. is also currently sidelined, which could leave Purdy with veteran Brandin Cooks as his top wideout. San Francisco is going to need firepower to keep pace with the pesky Falcons, who are led by Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Mike Kadlick Week 7 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+190) vs. New York Jets It’s time for the Dolphins to notch their first win of the Jeff Hafley era. While Miami currently owns the NFL’s worst offense and a bottom-10 defense, they’re coming off a bye week and are playing a Jets team that has lost four of its last five games. Though they’ve played competitively for the most part, New York has still yet to find an identity under coach Aaron Glenn and could be ripe for the taking after losing to the Patriots in Foxborough in Week 6. I think Miami finds their way to victory on Sunday at MetLife. Iain MacMillan Week 7 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+140) vs. Carolina Panthers It's time to sell high on this Panthers team. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face. Once they started facing top-10 defenses, I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate. I'm going to get in on the Bucs early this week and hope that Baker Mayfield ends up returning to action. If he starts on Sunday, we'll likely get some nice closing line value on the Buccaneers. Peter Dewey Week 7 Upset Pick Kansas City Chiefs (+124) vs. Seattle Seahawks This may be the biggest test for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs so far this season, as Seattle has the No. 1 defense in yards per play allowed and the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play. Yet, I’m taking Kansas City to win outright on the road and improve to 6-0. The Chiefs have found a new dynamic with Kenneth Walker III and this running game, and I expect the reigning Super Bowl MVP to have a major workload against his former team. Mahomes is a shocking 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up as a road underdog in his career, and he’s by far the better quarterback in this game. Sam Darnold has doomed Seattle at times this season, throwing seven picks in four games since returning from a glute injury. The Seahawks offense has been extremely reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and it ranks 25th in the league in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate. picks.headline: NFL straight-up picks, Week 7: Torn on Chiefs-Seahawks, doubting Lions moneyline
picks.blurb: The dynamic running back broke free of his platoon in Washington state after being deemed expendable despite the Seahawks' $700 million in contract extensions to keep its core intact. That made him the balm in a terribly burned Kansas City Chiefs backfield, where he's put up an Offensive Player of the Year pace across the team's 5-0 start. Now he faces his former team in his former home in primetime. That game has us torn in Week 7. It's not the only one. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 7 picks. Patriots at Bears Steelers at Saints Bengals at Ravens Browns at Titans Colts at Vikings Dolphins at Jets Giants at Texans 49ers at Falcons Bucs at Panthers Broncos at Cardinals Packers at Lions Rams at Raiders Chiefs at Seahawks Cowboys at Eagles Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: New York Jets (-4.5) over the Miami Dolphins Cool, I've murdered you once again. While I appreciate some Indianapolis Colts schadenfreude, I'm truly not enjoying this year's survivor slate. Ah well, time to back another flawed team with a quarterback working through yet another redemption arc. The Dolphins are coming off a bye and scored 24 points their last time out, but that was also the only week this season in which they've topped 13. New York's defense is competent. The Jets offense just got a boost with Omar Cooper Jr. returning to the lineup. Geno Smith faces the league's second-worst passing defense. If he can't thrive here, it's time to fade back into "high value backup" status. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 3-3 Hardest favorite to back: Baltimore Ravens (-1.5) over the Cincinnati Bengals Oh, friends, do I ever hate this pick. We're writing this on Wednesday and don't know what Lamar Jackson has planned for the week. If he's playing? I'm in. If not? This flips to Joe Shiesty and company. But, for now, let's assume we get an 80 percent Jackson behind center. Why I like this pick : The AFC North isn't defined by logic and answers only to the gods of chaos and violence. Baltimore has fielded the slightly better defense, and an emerging Ja'Kobi Lane brings an important fallback option. The Ravens find an extra gear against Cincinnati, beating the Bengals five of their last six tries and scoring at least 24 points in each of those wins. Why I don't like this pick : Even if Jackson plays, he'll have to face a revitalized and suddenly viable Bengals pass rush that has a strategy beyond "throw Trey Hendrickson at them, hope it works." The Bengals have the manpower to blitz effectively and the defensive backs to stand up in single coverage. Baltimore's top-heavy receiving corps will be put to the test, and it may take a Lane or a Devontez Walker to lift this team up in a high-scoring affair. Those Ravens wins came under Jim Harbaugh. Jesse Minter might be able to take up his mantle, but those are big shoes to fill seven weeks into his rookie season. Even worse, Cincinnati is coming off a bye. Season to date : 5-1 Upset pick of the week: Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) over the Seattle Seahawks Kenneth Walker III's respectful revenge game! The reigning Super Bowl MVP has been masterful at unclogging a previously stagnant Chiefs offense. Now he faces a defense he knows well. Will he leave Lumen Field with yet another win? The Chiefs are rolling right now. The Seahawks are not. The Super Bowl mainstay has rebounded from its uncharacteristic 2025 falloff by letting Walker cook. Kansas City has a top 10 passing offense in terms of expected points added (EPA) but is No. 1 by a wide margin when it comes to the run game . The Seahawks' run defense ranks third, which means this game is probably gonna be a pleasant reminder why we love this dumb sport so much. But Kansas City can counter with Patrick Mahomes. The Seahawks have Sam Darnold, who appears adrift without former coordinator Klint Kubiak, now head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders . Darnold's -0.050 EPA per dropback ranks 28th in the league. He's struggled to connect with anyone not named Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Chiefs have fielded a top four passing offense this season. Seattle's fans understand that, and they're going to be LOUD as evening descends on the Emerald City. The Chiefs have gotten better returns than expected from their receivers, but asking Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals to shine against the Seattle secondary is a monumental ask. Even in a 3-3 start the Seahawks defense ranks second only to the Minnesota Vikings in overall efficiency through six weeks. away.headline: Chiefs place Josh Simmons on IR, raising questions about his entire future in the NFL
away.blurb: Simmons has not played a down this season. He practiced in a limited capacity last week for the first time since reporting the injury to Burkholder. On Wednesday, the team listed him as a non-participant in practice for "back/non-injury personal reasons." In August, reporters close to the team repeatedly reported that the injury was minor and that Simmons would return by Week 1. He didn't. At this point, no one can reasonably assume Simmons will return this season after he becomes eligible. Likewise, the Chiefs cannot go into another year with Simmons as their unquestioned starting left tackle. The Kansas City Chiefs are placing left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, the team announced. But the story runs deeper than a Super Bowl contender losing its starting left tackle for, most likely, the remainder of the season. On Thursday, Chiefs Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rich Burkholder told reporters that Simmons reported a leg issue on August 17, which the team determined was related to a bulging disc in his back. Burkholder said Simmons saw a specialist who recommended therapy instead of surgery. Burkholder said Simmons used the day to speak with his family before deciding it would be best to go on injured reserve. The designation requires Simmons to miss at least four games. Put bluntly, skepticism about the Chiefs' version of events is warranted. The next explanation was that the Chiefs had not placed him on injured reserve because they expected him to play within the first four weeks. He never did. Burkholder says Simmons "plateaued" in his recovery. If so, head coach Andy Reid was unaware. On Monday, Reid said Simmons would continue to "ramp up" this week. On Wednesday morning, Reid did not include Simmons among the players who would not practice. The team's explanation is that Reid simply forgot to mention his starting left tackle's status. Simmons' history adds another mysterious element to the situation. In fact, "mysterious" was the word ESPN NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler used to describe it last month. Fowler's comment was notable because most other top national NFL reporters have avoided the story entirely. Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport host injury-related segments throughout the week on ESPN and NFL Network, yet neither has addressed the prolonged absence of Patrick Mahomes' starting left tackle. Meanwhile, they have provided countless updates on backup linebackers and kicker competitions. "Mysterious" also describes Simmons' rookie season a year ago. He missed an entire month due to what the team called a "personal matter." ESPN reported at the time that members of the organization were unaware of why Simmons did not show up before a Week 6 matchup against the Detroit Lions. In August, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame added that Simmons left the team the night before the game and that there was a period during which the team did not know his whereabouts. "It was decided and agreed upon by everybody — his people, his agent, him, myself, (Chiefs head coach) Andy (Reid), (general manager Brett) Veach — that he should be placed on IR to give him more time to return to full function." away.headline: Chiefs to place Josh Simmons on injured reserve; LT not eligible to return until Week 11
away.blurb: Simmons has been dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back and has not practiced yet this season. He was listed on Wednesday's injury report as being out with a back injury and for personal reasons, which Burkholder said was because Simmons took the rest of the day off after the decision was made to place him on injured reserve, per ESPN . Simmons was the Chiefs' first-round pick (No. 32 overall) in the 2025 NFL Draft . He played in just eight games during his rookie season, missing time for personal reasons in Weeks 6 through 9 and then suffering a dislocated and fractured wrist in Week 13 that knocked him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has been filling in for Simmons to start the season, and will presumably stick in the role at least until Simmons is eligible to return to the field in Week 11. Benson has been credited by Pro Football Focus with allowing 12 pressures through the first five games of the season, ranking 30th among 75 qualified tackles who have played at least 100 snaps. The Kansas City Chiefs will be without their starting left tackle for a while longer. Josh Simmons will be placed on injured reserve, according to Chiefs head trainer Rick Burkholder. "Josh worked his tail off and [was] diligent every day," Burkholder said, according to ESPN . "However, we feel he's plateaued in the rehab process. He's just not there yet." Burkholder did say that Simmons does not need surgery on the bulging disc, but that he simply needs more time to recover from the injury.

away.blurb: Charbonnet, who sustained a torn ACL that required surgery in a divisional-round playoff victory last season, was a full participant in practice Wednesday and might be able to return this weekend. Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Seahawks starting weakside linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle), who sat out last Thursday, missed practice on Wednesday. Fellow linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were among the players who were limited. Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) also missed practice. It remains unclear when left tackle Josh Simmons (back), who sat out Wednesday, will make his season debut. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. " ... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. And so it's all hands on deck to try to contain and try to stop him." His six rushing touchdowns are two behind Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, though he's played in one fewer game because of Kansas City's early bye week. Walker rushed for 135 yards on 27 carries in the Seahawks' 29-13 victory against New England in the Super Bowl. His desire to be a true No. 1, workhorse back led him to Kansas City after splitting carries with Zach Charbonnet during most of his time in Seattle. "He's wired to do it," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. "When you're on a team, everybody knows your strengths and weaknesses and quirks and everything. Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Seahawks starting weakside linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle), who sat out last Thursday, missed practice on Wednesday. Fellow linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were among the players who were limited. Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) also missed practice. It remains unclear when left tackle Josh Simmons (back), who sat out Wednesday, will make his season debut. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. " ... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. And so it's all hands on deck to try to contain and try to stop him." Walker, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs in the offseason as a free agent, leads all NFL running backs with 665 yards rushing and 6.3 yards per attempt. His six rushing touchdowns are two behind Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, though he's played in one fewer game because of Kansas City's early bye week. Walker rushed for 135 yards on 27 carries in the Seahawks' 29-13 victory against New England in the Super Bowl. His desire to be a true No. 1, workhorse back led him to Kansas City after splitting carries with Zach Charbonnet during most of his time in Seattle. "He's wired to do it," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. "When you're on a team, everybody knows your strengths and weaknesses and quirks and everything. I think the boys there will try to get after him a little bit. But he's a pretty level-headed guy. The way he plays, you're going to get a good rep when he gets the ball in his hands. home.headline: Chiefs’ Travis Kelce injury update is important for Week 7 Seahawks game
home.blurb: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury last week against the Chargers, and he's been listed as a limited participant in practice. Add ClutchPoints on Google Denny Medley-Imagn Images. The Kansas City Chiefs will be facing the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7, and they'll try to continue their undefeated streak this early in the season. Ahead of the game, the Chiefs are dealing with a few injuries, with one of the players being Travis Kelce . The tight end suffered an ankle injury during the first quarter of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers, but he was still able to gut it out and play through it. Kelce was limited in practice on Wednesday, and on Thursday he was limited as well , according to the Chiefs. “Travis Kelce, Cooper McDonald, L'Jarius Sneed, and Brashard Smith were limited in practice today. Jaylon Moore and Rashee Rice did not practice,” the Chiefs wrote on X, formerly Twitter. All eyes will be on Kelce's participation in practice tomorrow, and he may end up being questionable for the matchup against the Seahawks. As of now, it looks like Kelce has a good chance of playing, but anything can happen between now and game day. That means everyone will have to step up, and it should be a good matchup between the two teams. This game is also going to be special for Kenneth Walker III, as he faces off against his former team. Walker won Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks last season, but there was a chance that they weren't going to be able to pay him the money he wanted in free agency. That led to him signing with the Chiefs, and so far, it's safe to say that he's been in league MVP conversations with the way he's running the ball. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 7 vs. Seattle Seahawks includes a new twist in the ongoing Josh Simmons saga
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. After being a limited participant in practice all of last week with a back injury, Chiefs starting LT Josh Simmons is back to being a non-participant. The difference this time? Simmons is now being listed with both the back injury and a “personal” designation. You might recall the 2025 NFL season, when Simmons missed four weeks due to a personal family matter. When he returned, Simmons broke his wrist and ultimately played in just eight total games that year. It's unclear what the “personal” designation refers to, but The Athletic's Jesse Newell said Simmons was in the locker room ahead of practice . Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's Week 7 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 23. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Cooper McDonald was limited in his first practice back since returning from injured reserve . This is part of the normal ramp-up process. Travis Kelce is listed as limited after “tweaking” his ankle in Week 6's game against the Chargers. I expected this for the veteran , but I don't anticipate him being at risk of missing Sunday's game. home.blurb: Zach Charbonnet , who has a chance to return from the physically unable to perform list this week, was a full participant for the first time since returning to practice earlier this month. Another player the Seahawks are hoping to get back, right guard Anthony Bradford , was listed as limited in his first practice since going on injured reserve earlier this season. Also limited for the Seahawks were linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique), who started in place of Thomas last week, receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed (hip), guard Beau Stephens (knee) and quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow). For the Chiefs, right tackle Jaylon Moore did not practice due to a concussion, while left tackle Josh Simmon was a non-participant due to a personal matter. Also sidelined on Wednesday was receiver Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring). home.headline: Chiefs-Seahawks Week 7 Thursday injury report: Rashee Rice stays sidelined
home.blurb: On Thursday, Kansas City placed left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) on the Reserve/Injured list after he didn't practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs explained that Simmons plateaued in his rehabilitation and needed more time to return to 100%. For more information from the team's Head Trainer Rick Burkholder, we covered his statement to local media here . Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore's participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player's hands. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team's Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been "designated to return," McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Linebacker Tyrice Knight, former Missouri quarterback Drew Lock, wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip) and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were limited particpants in Wednesday's practice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Cowboys vs. Eagles Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Cowboys -4.5 (-112) Eagles +4.5 (-108) Cowboys: -225 44.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Dallas opened as a 5.5-point favorite for Monday night’s showdown , but that line has quickly shifted towards the Eagles. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys were figured to be the two frontrunners in the NFC East this season, with some even considering the duo as Super Bowl contenders. Just six weeks into the season, both teams are closer to booking vacations than they are preparing for a February trip to Los Angeles. Injuries did a number on the Eagles, claiming Saquon Barkley and many more. Recently, Jalen Hurts was added to that list. The quarterback is done for the year with blood clots . As for Dallas, it's still the defense. And it always has been. In recent weeks, though, the Cowboys offense has become a major problem as well. That isn't a winning combination for Brian Schottenheimer, who has seen his job security come into question lately. Both teams are desperate for a win, but at least the Eagles have a built-in excuse. Dallas will try to right the ship, but can they do it in a hostile Philadelphia environment? Eagles vs Cowboys odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -3 Moneyline: Eagles -162; Cowboys +136 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Eagles Keys To Victory Stay in the fight. For all intents and purposes, the Eagles season is over after it was revealed Jalen Hurts would miss the remainder of the campaign with blood clots. Injuries have mounted, but there is still talent on this Philadelphia roster. And with the way Dallas is playing, the Eagles just have to stick around long enough to let the Cowboys beat themselves. That leaky defense and anemic offense will give the home team plenty of opportunities to win. The Eagles just have to take them. Cowboys Keys To Victory Show up. On paper, Dallas should run away with this game against an offense that can't possibly keep up. However, the Cowboys looked disinterested in Week 6 and have looked that way for quite some time. This is the perfect get-right spot against a division rival. If the Cowboys don't beat themselves, they'll win the game. Injuries to watch • RB Saquon Barkley • OL Landon Dickerson • DL Jordan Davis • LB Nolan Smith • LB Jaylx Hunt • WR KaVontae Turpin • LB DeMarvion Overshown • LB Dee Winters Eagles vs Cowboys USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Eagles 23, Cowboys 17 The Eagles are injured. The Cowboys are lifeless. One of them has to win. How's that for a promo? Dallas is clearly the more talented team on paper, but something stinks about this group, and it's hard to pinpoint where the smell is coming from. The defense isn't competitive. The offense appears to be going through the motions. After a rough week for the Eagles, they should be motivated to stop the bleeding and get back in the win column. And what better way to do that than against a hated rival? Even if it's only for a moment, the home team finally gives the fans a reason to smile. Adam Kaufman: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20 Not sure how many times I'm going to put myself in position to be let down by the Cowboys this season, but here we are again. With Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles need Tanner McKee to stabilize an offense that was already having problems. Dallas' vulnerable defense – to put it kindly – gives him an opportunity, especially if Philadelphia can establish the run. On the other side, Dak Prescott's offense has been largely absent each of the last two weeks. But the superior talent undeniably belongs to the Cowboys and, if they can protect the ball, I like them to bounce back in a pivotal division matchup. away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. home.headline: Eagles not punished by NFL for handling of Jalen Hurts blood clots, per reports; NFLPA says more investigation needed
home.blurb: It was revealed Monday that Hurts will be out indefinitely after multiple clots were discovered in his lungs. The news came two days after Hurts was placed on injured reserve — despite initial reports stating the team wouldn’t place him on IR — and four days after last week’s announcement that he had a blood clot in his calf. “I fully trust the people that are involved in helping us all make these decisions,” Sirianni said. “We have great people here. … The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them. “Don’t have much more to say about that. That’s why we put the statement out. Full trust in those guys … kind of feels like you’re questioning that, and I know you guys have a job to do, but I’ve got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other. So, it’s always at the forefront of our mind.” The Eagles won’t face any heat from the NFL for their handling of Jalen Hurts’ potentially season-ending injury. The NFL concluded, in news first reported by The Athletic and later confirmed by the Associated Press, that the Eagles clearing Hurts to play in Week 5 despite having a superficial blood clot in his calf was “handled appropriately.” The league will not be issuing any punishment for their handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation for the game. Later on Tuesday, the NFL Players Association issued a statement: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” The Eagles’ medical staff has faced scrutiny from fans and media for its handling of the Hurts situation. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners.
